newsitem.title: CHINA: China Shougang '96 profits to hit 320 million yuan.
newsitem.headline: China Shougang '96 profits to hit 320 million yuan.

text.p: Pre-tax profits of the Capital Iron and Steel Group (Shougang) are expected to hit 320 million yuan in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The profits for 1996 would outstrip the group's target by 6.67 percent, it said, but gave no details or comparative figures.
Sales of Shougang would reach 22.16 billion yuan in 1996, with a sales to production ratio of 101.3 percent, it said.
Shougang's rolled steel production was expected to reach 6.89 million tonnes in 1996, up 3.56 percent over 1995. Iron production was expected to reach 7.296 million tonnes, up by 1.4 percent.
The Beijing steel giant said in November it had restructured into a business group with 27 subsidiaries.
Shougang had cut production costs by 539 million yuan in 1996 compared with 1995 by reducing expenditure and tightening management, Xinhua said.
Stockpiles of steel ingots, rolled steel and billet fell by 51,700 tonnes from the start of the year, it said.
However, Shougang had faced difficult market conditions in 1996 because of rising prices of raw materials as well as higher electricity and transport costs, it said.
